theme: Democrats sweep the midterms and AI-rule fears hit stocks: the Nasdaq has its worst day since April 2025, chips, Tesla and SpaceX drop about 10%, Korea and Taiwan tumble, bitcoin ETFs see outflows but BTC holds $75K, and Anthropic's $895B commitments are in focus.

items.title: How much bitcoin US spot ETFs hold, by fund
items.picked: US bitcoin and ether ETFs saw about $530M of outflows on Nov 5 as the Nasdaq fell 5.5%, with BlackRock among the sellers, per stories trending on X. Bitcoin still held above $75,000 after the Binance hack and the midterm selloff.
items.matters: ETF holdings are the biggest pool of bitcoin demand from regular investors. Outflows show how much of that demand leaves when stocks sell off.
items.know: The tab has 1,283,681 BTC across 12 US spot ETFs as of Oct 16, 2026, down from 1,292,081 in April. BlackRock's IBIT holds 803,871 BTC and Fidelity's FBTC 177,542. The data is about three weeks old and does not include this week's outflows.

items.title: Bitcoin vs Nasdaq: 90-day correlation of daily returns
items.picked: The Nasdaq had its worst day since April 2025 on Nov 5 on fears of AI rules after the Democratic midterm sweep. Bitcoin dipped but held above $75,000, and X posts called it resilient.
items.matters: The more bitcoin moves with tech stocks, the less it works as a diversifier. A tech selloff then tends to pull it down too.
items.know: The 90-day correlation was 0.408 in the week of Oct 29, 2026, with bitcoin at $77,939. It was 0.433 on Oct 9 and 0.076 in January 2019. The data ends Oct 29, before this week's selloff.

items.title: Tesla's 1-year beta and correlation to the Nasdaq-100
items.picked: Tesla fell 10.8% to $343.69 on Nov 5 while the Nasdaq dropped 5.5%, after Democrats took Congress. Retail traders on X called it a dip to buy.
items.matters: Beta shows how much Tesla tends to move for each 1% move in the Nasdaq-100. A high beta means tech selloffs hit Tesla harder.
items.know: The tab has Tesla's 1-year beta at 1.466 and its correlation at 0.654 as of Oct 30, 2026. Beta was 1.561 in mid-September and 1.084 in January 2019. The data ends Oct 30, before Thursday's drop.

items.title: SpaceX (SPCX) price-to-sales since its listing
items.picked: SpaceX closed at $123.62 on Nov 5, below its $135 IPO price, after a roughly 9% drop. ARK Invest bought shares on the dip, per stories trending on X.
items.matters: Price-to-sales shows how much investors pay for each dollar of SpaceX revenue. It tracks how much growth is priced in as the stock swings.
items.know: On Oct 30, 2026, the tab has SPCX at $134.72, a $1,775.85B market cap and $23.04B of trailing 4-quarter revenue, or 77.08x sales. That is down from 131.47x on Jun 15. The data ends Oct 30, before this week's drop below $124.

items.title: OpenAI vs Anthropic: reported annualized revenue run-rate
items.picked: Anthropic's amended IPO filing, trending on X, lists $895B of compute and data center commitments. That puts its revenue growth next to its spending.
items.matters: Revenue at the AI labs is what pays for the data center buildout behind Nvidia, the neoclouds and the hyperscalers.
items.know: The tab has Anthropic's reported run-rate at $100B in Sep 2026, up from $1B in Dec 2024 and $9B in Dec 2025. OpenAI's latest entry is $70B in Sep 2026, up from $20B in Dec 2025. These are reported run-rates, and the dates are uneven.

items.title: Nvidia's supply and capacity commitments by fiscal quarter
items.picked: Nvidia closed at $181.60 on Nov 5, down over 9%, on fears of slower AI data center spending, then rose about 5% premarket on Nov 6, per X.
items.matters: Supply commitments are what Nvidia has promised to buy from suppliers. They show how big a buildout it is planning for, and what it is on the hook for if demand slows.
items.know: The tab has $279B of supply and capacity commitments at the Jul 26, 2026 quarter end, up from $119B in April and $95.2B in January. That is about 9x the $30.8B in January 2025. The next 10-Q is not in the tab yet.

items.title: Micron quarterly revenue and gross margin
items.picked: Micron fell more than 17% on Nov 5 and was up over 9% premarket on Nov 6. Investors on X are debating whether memory makers' long-term supply deals will hold up in a downturn.
items.matters: Memory is the most cyclical part of the AI chip trade. Margins this high have not lasted in past cycles.
items.know: The tab has quarterly revenue of $54.23B with an 86.8% gross margin for Sep 2026, up from $11.32B and 44.67% in Sep 2025. In the 2016 trough, margins were under 20%. The latest quarter is Sep 2026.

items.title: Semiconductors vs the S&P 500, and the SOXX drawdown
items.picked: Chip stocks led Thursday's rout, with AMD and Micron down more than 17%. Edward Dowd's post that semis are down 32% from June peaks is trending on X.
items.matters: Semis have led this market. When they lose ground to the S&P 500, the AI trade is losing momentum.
items.know: The tab has semis vs the S&P 500 at 237.89 in Oct 2026 (Jul 2001 = 100), down from 327.76 in June. The SOXX total-return drawdown was -26.37% at end of October. The data is monthly through October, so it does not include this week's drop.

items.title: South Korea and Taiwan stocks relative to the S&P 500
items.picked: Korea's Kospi fell 8.8% and Taiwan's TAIEX 9% after the US tech selloff, led by Samsung, SK Hynix and TSMC, per X news.
items.matters: Korea and Taiwan are the chip and memory supply chain. They are the purest overseas bets on AI hardware.
items.know: The tab has Korea vs the S&P 500 at 161.58 in Oct 2026 (Jan 2001 = 100), down from 218.41 in May. Taiwan was at 101.35, down from 112.14 in September. The data is monthly through October, before this week's drop.

items.title: VIX term structure: 3-month VIX divided by VIX
items.picked: Thursday's 4.4% S&P 500 drop sent volatility higher. Traders are watching today's October jobs report to see if Friday's chip rebound holds.
items.matters: When the ratio falls below 1, near-term fear is above longer-term fear. That has often marked stress peaks.
items.know: The tab's last October reading is 1.126, with VIX at 17.2 and VIX3M at 19.37. An earlier October reading hit 1.053 with VIX at 19.45. The data ends in late October and does not include this week's selloff.
